title: Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for AI Security

blocks.text: This guide explains the configuration steps that you need to complete to begin using AI Security for your organization.
Before you begin configuring AI Security, Zscaler recommends reading the following article:
To configure AI Security, complete the following steps:

blocks.item: After your organization is provisioned for AI Security, you receive an email to complete the registration. To learn more, see Signing in to the AI Security Admin Portal.
Step 2: Set up the DLP Engines and Define Sensitive Data
AI Security uses predefined DLP engines and dictionaries that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA) to classify data types. To learn more, see Understanding DLP Engines and Dictionaries.

You can onboard the Amazon Web Services (AWS) organizations, Microsoft Azure tenants, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP) organizations into AI Security. When onboarded, AI Security monitors the data in your cloud accounts for any vulnerabilities and threats and provides comprehensive reports of your data's security posture. To learn more, see About Cloud Accounts.

After you have onboarded the cloud accounts, you need to configure the scan settings. AI Security scans the resources (data stores, cloud storage, virtual machines, etc.) in your onboarded cloud accounts, classifies the data, detects vulnerabilities, and generates alerts so you can evaluate the issue and take necessary action. To learn more, see About Scan Settings.
You need to add users and user groups and assign roles in the Zscaler Admin Console to control their level of access to specific modules. To learn more, see About Users.

You can onboard your cloud accounts and map them to business units. You can restrict user access to specific business units. For example, you might want to restrict a group to Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts or restrict partners to view resources only in a specific account. To learn more, see About Business Units.
Step 7: Configure the AI Posture Policies

AI Security offers predefined data posture policies to meet your organization's compliance requirements across multiple cloud service providers (CSPs). You can also create custom policies. To learn more, see About AI Posture Policies.

You can configure and manage alert rules and notifications, so individuals in your organization can receive notifications for any security policy violations that occur in your cloud resources. To learn more, see About Issues.
Step 9: Configure External Integrations and Notifications

AI Security offers incident management by integrating with IT Service Management (ITSM) tools and cloud storage services. You can send alert data to these tools for further investigation and remediation. To learn more, see About External Integrations.
